key_insight: The paper argues that long-horizon agents don’t just need more memory—they need the right memory to be brought back at the right time. It introduces proactive memory as an active mechanism to prevent “behavioral state decay” when important task details get buried or lost in long trajectories.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of long-horizon decision-making where critical information such as prior attempts, task requirements, environment facts, and open subgoals becomes hard to access as the context grows.
method: Uses a separate memory agent to proactively identify decision-relevant state instead of relying only on passive retrieval.
Surfaces buried information from the expanding trajectory before it is needed, helping the action agent stay aligned with current goals.
Targets behavioral state decay by maintaining continuity of task context across long sequences of actions and observations.
impact: This matters because long-context agents often fail not from lack of information, but from failing to recall the right information at the right moment. Proactive memory can improve reliability, planning, and recovery in real-world long-horizon tasks.

paper_title: Remember When It Matters: Proactive Memory Agent for Long-Horizon Agents
paper_authors: Yifan Wu, Lizhu Zhang, Yuhang Zhou, Mingyi Wang, Bo Peng
